newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares rebound in half-hearted fashion.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares rebound in half-hearted fashion.

text.p: Belgian shares regained their footing on Tuesday morning after two consecutive sessions of heavy losses, but traders said the recovery was patchy.

The main beneficiaries were recent big losers, such as bank BBL, up 190 francs, or 2.09 percent, at 9,260 francs, one trader said. But six of the 20 Bel-20 index components remained stuck in negative territory.

One trader said that although external factors, such as long-term interest rates and the dollar, remained positive, some smaller investors reading newspaper headlines about the bourse's drop on Monday may have decided to take profit.
The Bel-20 was up 0.39 percent at 2,479.86 points, off its high of the day, but still up 31 percent on its level at the end of 1996.
Retailer Colruyt was up 2.86 percent at 18,000 francs. Chemicals and drugs maker UCB was up 2.40 percent at 128,000 francs.
Among foreign issues, Luxembourg-based steel maker Arbed was up 130 francs, or 2.9 percent, at 4,610 francs.

Dealers said investors continued to welcome news of the company's acquisition of a minority stake in Spanish state steel maker CSI. -- Nick Antonovics, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6817, Fax +32 2 230 7710
